task: Task 2 — Real-Browser Keyboard and Accessibility Verification
scope: Characterization only. No production change. Genuine trusted keyboard input via Playwright; assertions read public-observable DOM + the Chromium accessibility tree (CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree). Discrepancies are characterized, never repaired.

browser.determinism: single project (chromium), workers=1, fullyParallel=false, retries=0, headless=true

harness.systemUnderTest: vanilla-demo (http://localhost:5173/vanilla-demo.html) with enhanced-select / select-option custom elements; demo's own static selects purged so the AX tree contains only suite-mounted instances
harness.inputModel: Playwright locator.press / focus deliver genuine trusted keyboard events (NOT synthetic KeyboardEvent dispatch)
harness.proxyNote: NO_PROXY for localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 is enforced in-config so webServer probes do not traverse the developer outbound proxy
harness.whyChrome1248: The repo pins @playwright/test 1.59.1 whose default Chromium (revision 1217) is geo-blocked on this environment's CDN (HTTP 403). The cache already carries a full Chrome-for-Testing build (chromium-1248) which supports CDP AX tree + ariaSnapshot; Playwright is pointed at it explicitly for reproducibility.

T2-01.title: Browser harness (deterministic Chromium, version recorded)
findings: Chromium engine version is reported at 156.0.8078.4 (matches /^\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/).
Mounted combobox renders with role=combobox and aria-expanded=false initially.
Initial mount is closed (no data-open) with no aria-activedescendant.

T2-02.title: Keyboard navigation (Arrow/Home/End/Page/Enter/Space)
findings: ArrowDown on a closed+focused combobox opens it AND pre-activates the first option (aria-activedescendant -> 'a').
ArrowDown/ArrowUp move one selectable step and skip a disabled option (a -> c -> a).
ArrowDown/ArrowUp clamp at the first/last selectable option (no wrap-around).
Home jumps to first selectable (a); End jumps to last selectable (d).
PageDown/PageUp move by 10 selectable options (v0 -> v10; v24 -> v14).
Enter activates the active option and closes; Space activates the pre-active option in the non-searchable default.

T2-03.title: Popup dismissal (Escape/Tab/focus transfer/close chronology)
findings: Escape closes an open popup and sets aria-expanded=false.
Tab closes an open popup but does NOT advance DOM focus to the next tabbable; document.activeElement falls back to BODY (recorded as P1.3-D04; not repaired).
Escape and Tab both emit close with empty detail ({}); indistinguishable — confirms P1.3-D01 in a real browser.
Escape/Tab while already closed emit no close event.

T2-04.title: DOM focus (document.activeElement + shadow root)
findings: DOM focus is on the ENHANCED-SELECT host; the shadow active element is the combobox input (part=input).
Focus stays on the input across open + arrow movement; the active option is expressed via aria-activedescendant, never via DOM focus.
Escape leaves DOM focus on the combobox input.

T2-05.title: ARIA relationships (combobox/listbox/option/aria-controls/expanded/activedescendant)
findings: combobox aria-controls equals the listbox id (aria-owns also present).
aria-expanded reflects open/closed; aria-activedescendant resolves to an option.
AX tree exposes a combobox with hasPopup=listbox and controls, plus >=1 listbox role.

T2-06.title: Disabled options (keyboard exclusion + a11y state)
findings: A disabled option is never activated by keyboard traversal (ArrowUp/Down sweep never lands on 'b').
Disabled option exposes aria-disabled=true in the DOM and disabled=true state in the AX tree ('Bravo').

T2-07.title: Selection policies (single/multi/allowDeselect/maxSelections, keyboard-only)
findings: Single mode: Enter selects the active option and closes.
Multi + allowDeselect: Enter toggles a selection off; multi opens with NO pre-active option.
maxSelections caps keyboard selections (second Enter rejected).
Multi-select listbox exposes aria-multiselectable=true.

T2-08.title: Accessibility representation (Chromium AX tree)
findings: Selected option in multi mode is exposed with AX property selected=true. NOTE: a selected option carries a chip remove affordance so its accessible name is '<label> Remove option' (e.g. 'Alpha Remove option'), not the bare label. This is correct behavior (select-option.ts:427 aria-label='Remove option'); the assertion matches by label prefix.
Combobox accessible name derives from a host aria-label ('Favorite color').
aria-activedescendant is reported as a related-node idref on the combobox AX node.

T2-09.title: Reassessment of P1.3-D01/D02/D03 with browser evidence
findings: D01: public close detail is {} in the browser; Escape and Tab indistinguishable — CONFIRMED.

D02: legacy host aria-busy is inert on the listbox (null) BY DESIGN; genuine busy (public load-more click -> _setBusy(true)) DOES reflect aria-busy='true' onto the listbox — RESOLVED (reflection target = listbox; works when actually busy; the jsdom 'missing' was the inert legacy attribute, not a defect).
D03: keyboard-open pre-activates the first option in the browser (jsdom Task-1 'no initial active' was a jsdom artifact) — REASSESSED.

T2-10.title: Regression / harness integrity (browser path uses public surface only)
findings: A complete open -> move -> select cycle is driven entirely through real keyboard input on the public surface; no private-method assertion helpers.

P1.3-D01.detail: CloseEventDetail is empty {}; Escape and Tab both emit close:{} in Chromium. No close reason surfaced. Disposition unchanged: characterized, design decision deferred; no production change; no ADR.
P1.3-D01.evidence: T2-03 close-detail tests + T2-09 D01 test

P1.3-D02.detail: The listbox IS the aria-busy reflection target and it receives aria-busy='true' when the component is genuinely busy (public load-more click -> _setBusy(true)). The legacy host aria-busy attribute is intentionally inert for listbox semantics (in-code comment in _syncListboxAccessibility). The Task-1 jsdom observation tested the inert legacy attribute, which is NOT a limitation: real busy state is correctly exposed on the listbox. Chromium exposes the busy state on the listbox node when active.
sourceReferences: packages/core/src/platform/web/accessibility-effects.ts (applyListbox sets aria-busy on listbox when effect.busy)
packages/core/src/components/enhanced-select.ts _syncListboxAccessibility (~4294) — sets busy only when isBusy || (protocol==='acknowledged' && host aria-busy==='true')
P1.3-D02.recommendation: Downgrade D02 from 'Diagnostic / pending' to 'Resolved — reflection target is the listbox; verified when genuinely busy'. No production change.
P1.3-D02.evidence: T2-09 D02 test (legacy inert + genuine busy reflects)

P1.3-D03.detail: In Chromium, keyboard-open pre-activates the first selectable option (aria-activedescendant -> first). The Task-1 jsdom 'opening assigns no initial aria-activedescendant' result does not reproduce in a real browser, so it is a jsdom artifact rather than a genuine conformance gap. Real-browser behavior aligns with the APG default-ish pattern (first option pre-active). Multi mode, by contrast, opens with NO pre-active option (also observed).
P1.3-D03.apgNote: Difference from an APG example is not, by itself, nonconformance. Recorded as observation; no defect asserted.
P1.3-D03.evidence: T2-02 ArrowDown-open test + T2-09 D03 test

P1.3-D04.summary: Tab closes the popup but does NOT advance DOM focus to the next tabbable control.
P1.3-D04.detail: When the combobox is open and Tab is pressed, the popup closes (close event, aria-expanded=false) but DOM focus does not move to the next focusable element; document.activeElement falls back to BODY rather than the following button. Recorded as an observation, not repaired. Whether Tab should transfer focus onward (default Tab navigation) is a design decision for future a11y work.
P1.3-D04.risk: Keyboard users pressing Tab to leave an open combobox may not land on the expected next control and could lose their place.
P1.3-D04.disposition: Characterized, not repaired. No production change; no ADR during W1-P1.
P1.3-D04.evidence: T2-03 'Tab closes an open popup (observed: focus does NOT advance...)'

AX-selected-option-name.summary: A selected option in multi mode has an accessible name suffixed with 'Remove option'.
AX-selected-option-name.detail: select-option.ts:427 gives the chip remove button aria-label='Remove option'; the composed option AX name becomes '<label> Remove option'. Selection is exposed via the AX 'selected' property (true). This is correct; the T2-08 assertion matches by label prefix.

coverageImplications.note: Browser evidence justifies the following status clarifications in the W1-P1.3 traceability/ledger narrative. The traceability record count (112: Existing 38 / Partial 29 / Diagnostic 41 / Missing 4) is NOT changed by Task 2; only per-record notes for D01/D02/D03 are updated where justified.
coverageImplications.P1.3-D02: Diagnostic -> effectively resolved (listbox is the reflection target and receives aria-busy when genuinely busy). The Diagnostic guard test remains in the jsdom suite (Task 1) and the browser evidence now confirms the behavior.
coverageImplications.P1.3-D03: Observation -> browser confirms first-option pre-activation on keyboard open; the jsdom 'no initial active' is an artifact. No behavior change.
coverageImplications.P1.3-D01: Confirmed in browser; remains a documented public-contract limitation.
coverageImplications.P1.3-D04: New observation added (Tab does not advance focus).

productionIsolation.statement: No files under packages/core/src, packages/core/engine, or packages/core/adapters were modified.
